Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement

How PLLA Is Prepared and Injected: Why Technique Matters

With PLLA, preparation and placement matter as much as the product itself. Breast-specific protocols are not standardised.

Home/Non-Surgical Breast Enlargement/Sculptra and PLLA/How PLLA Is Prepared and Injected: Why Technique Matters

With PLLA, how the product is prepared and placed matters as much as the product itself. This page is part of our guide to Sculptra and PLLA.

Reconstitution and dilution

The powder is mixed with sterile water and sometimes anaesthetic. Different clinicians use different volumes. More dilute mixtures are often used for broader areas such as the body or chest. Product instructions describe a specific preparation, and following them is important. Some practitioners deviate based on experience, which may or may not be supported by evidence.

Rest time

The mixture is often left to hydrate before use. Skipping this step may affect how it behaves and may affect the evenness of particle distribution.

Injection technique

PLLA can be placed at different depths using needles or cannulas, in fan-like or crosshatch patterns. Placement that is too superficial can raise the chance of palpable or visible nodules. Technique should be appropriate to the exact product, area and treatment goal.

Massage

Practitioners often recommend massaging the treated area for several days to spread the product, but protocols vary. Follow the written advice from the clinician who knows the product and technique used.

Session spacing

Treatment is usually given in a series of sessions spaced weeks apart rather than all at once. Early repeat treatment before the tissue response is clear can add cost and risk without showing whether the initial treatment helped.

Why this matters for you

Because practice varies and breast-specific protocols are not standardised, outcomes depend heavily on the clinician’s training and judgement. Ask about their experience and the exact method proposed.

Questions to ask

  • How do you prepare and dilute the product?
  • What depth and technique will you use?
  • How many sessions do you recommend, and why?
  • What aftercare do you advise?

Key takeaway

Technique affects safety, so ask for specifics and credentials.
